hypothesis: The model has no representation of an Army institution refusing a lawful civilian order (contract 1.1). Implementing the decided mechanism adds that cause of conflict over civilian executive authority, which a player can see and influence.
prediction: None. The effect on A1 and on every other gate is unknown until measured. It may be zero or negative. No A1 value or direction is written here, for any scope, price, rule or temperament (contract 1.3). Nothing in this plan was chosen by its effect on seeds 0-11.
structural_note_not_a_prediction:
This is a property of the decided design, stated so the measurement is read correctly.
- Under Q1(a) Prudent, ai_order and the order's arm read the same state in the same tick, so every AI order is accepted at issue (contract 11.2-11.3).
- The census has no player, so no dispute, enforcement or escalation can arise in it.
- Any census change can therefore come only through compliance: lower leverage and saved powers.
- It can also come through the world-path effects in the contract's section 16: new draws on the single RNG stream, the order taking a candidate slot in ticks with no lever and no card, and political-capital spending.
Diagnostic D3 checks this directly: a nonzero count of AI-issued refusals is an implementation bug.

change.Q2_Q3: Q2 (a) and Q3 (b). The order rides the existing single draw, `w.rng.chance(clock::chance(w, 0.02))` in stratagems::ai_stratagems, as a third candidate. It is consulted only when government::ai_lever returns None and no card is chosen, so the precedence is lever, then card, then order. Unchanged: ai_lever, the card choice, the 0.02 draw and its position, and one decision per actor per tick. There is no new draw site. In every tick where ai_order returns None, the control flow and the draws equal the base exactly.
change.Q4:
(b) While Enforced, gap = min(0.35 - dispute_acceptance(current scope), 0.45 * leverage * s), where leverage = civilian_army_executive_leverage(w, id) read at the tick and s is the current scope's stake.
- Accrual: when gap > 0, authority_pressure = min(1.5, authority_pressure + 0.60 * gap * dt), with dt = clock::month_fraction(w).
- There is no discontent term and no cooling; the gauge lives in the record and is deleted on every closure. It never reads or writes GovState.coup_pressure.
- Route 2 is untouched: electoral_army_tick, maybe_electoral_coup, the live D >= .25 and eff < .35 guards, the 12-month settled rule, and the rate and cap.
- Firing (contract 10.3) needs all of: ideology_takeover; status Enforced; dispute_acceptance < .35; electoral_coup_settled_months >= 12 and !awaiting_first_election; a passed validation (the issuer governs, the state is electoral, authoritarianism > .20, the institution exists, rules 5-6 hold); and authority_pressure >= 1/crisis_intensity.max(0.1).
change.Q5:
(b) Nothing closes a dispute in compliance during the tick. Contract 9.4, and step 3 of the 10.1 tick, are not implemented. A dispute closes in compliance only inside an explicit government action:
- Negotiate re-tests at the narrower scope and closes as NegotiatedCompliance;
- Enforce re-tests at the current scope and closes as CompliedWhileOpen (reading R2).
Funding keeps its material benefit, a higher acceptance. While acceptance >= .35, the gap is <= 0, so nothing accrues and the dispute cannot fire, but the record stays open until the government acts. The hysteresis question is moot.
change.Q6:
(b) A new saved field holds complied scopes as institutional powers: GovState.civilian_powers: Vec<CivilianPower { institution: InstitutionRef, scope: AuthorityScope, since: Date }>. It is serde default, skipped when empty, and a strict type.
- Each compliance (Complied, NegotiatedCompliance, CompliedWhileOpen) records the power and calls army_authority::consolidate_transfer(w, id, 0.05 * s), unchanged, once.
- A new legality rule, after rule 11 and before rule 12, refuses an order for a saved (institution, scope): "{institution} already accepts {phrase}."
- Negotiation steps down to the next narrower scope that is not saved.
See reading R3.
change.Q8: (b) Legality rule 5 holds when (g.elected && g.unrestricted_mandate && !g.awaiting_first_election) || opening_mandates::attested_parties(w, id).is_some(). attested_parties already requires the sourced marker, an unchanged catalogue row, no bans, no awaited first ballot, the leader's party among the attested parties, and the sourced office. Rule 6, an established six-month record of the current party, is unchanged and still required. See reading R11.
change.Q9:
(a) and (c).
Prices (unchanged):
- AssertCivilianAuthority: 25 PC, REFUSABLE, charged once the arm returns Ok, whether the institution complies or refuses.
- Withdraw: 12 PC, ALWAYS, to the point of bankruptcy.
- Negotiate: 0 PC.
- Enforce: 0 PC up front, plus 0.20 PC a month while Enforced.
AI reserve: the AI issues only when political_capital >= 25 + AI_ORDER_RESERVE_PC (68), i.e. >= 93. See reading R4.
change.Q10:
(a) and (d). Rule 13 refuses an order only when both of these hold:
- the newest receipt's order.issuer equals the current governing-party key ("party:<leader>");
- clock::month_index(now) - month_index(closed_on) < 12.
A receipt from another issuer never binds, so the cooldown resets when the issuer is replaced. See reading R5.
change.Q11: (b) A Negotiate that still refuses rescales the pressure to the narrower scope's gap: authority_pressure = min(1.5, authority_pressure * gap_narrow / gap_wide). Both gaps are the Q4 gaps at the action's state, and the result is 0 when gap_wide <= 0. The dispute then returns to Refused with a new decision window, and nothing accrues while Refused.
change.Q12:
(b) When the dispute tick finds an Enforced dispute whose political capital cannot pay that tick's upkeep in full (political_capital < 0.20 * dt), the dispute closes as Withdrawn and does not accrue or fire.
- The withdrawal price is charged under ALWAYS, floored at 0.
- It prints the withdrawal headline, and the cooldown starts at closure.
See reading R6.
change.Q13: (b) and (c). The escalation calls the existing break_electoral, unchanged, with the route-2 template plus a census-compatible suffix: "COUP IN {NATION}: {institution} removes the elected government that ordered {phrase}." No fifth takeover-watch road or gauge is added. See reading R7.

change.Q15: (a) Three Army-only scopes, with invented stakes: BudgetOversight 1/3, SeniorAppointments 2/3, CivilianCommand 1.
change.Q16: (a) Reuse the programme veto's weight, ARMY_PROGRAMME_VETO_WEIGHT = .45, through a shared pure helper. army_programme_veto_loyalty keeps the identical operation order, and both Algeria chronology tests pass unmodified.
change.Q17: (a) The decision window is the refusal month plus the whole following calendar month (Refused { decide_by_month: month_index + 1 }). At the first dispute tick with month_index > decide_by_month, the order stands as Enforced (StepKind::EnforcedByDefault).
change.Q18: (a) Route 2's .60 slope with no floor, applied to the Q4 gap, with a cap of 1.5. No public-mandate slowing and no maximum duration.
change.Q19: (a) Closed entirely while ideology_takeover is off. Browser play's government payload and every existing web test's action list stay byte-identical.
change.Q20: (a) One national leverage. A break reseats institutions as regime_break already does.
change.Q21: (a) A withdrawal costs political capital only. Leverage, loyalty and authoritarianism are unchanged.
change.Q22:
(a) A dispute loaded into a takeover-off world is frozen.
- The validation step, the dispute tick and the regime_break hook are all gated on both switches, so a maybe_coup break with takeover off leaves the frozen record untouched.
- Resolutions are refused by the switch sentence, and the browser does not show the dispute.

change.Q23: (a) A new resolution variant, Resolution::MandateLapsed, is validation row 6, after InstitutionGone. It applies when legality rule 5 or 6 no longer holds while the state is still electoral. dispute_acceptance is total on every record that passes validation (I16, control 34). See reading R8.
change.Q24: (b) When the issuing government exits by its own suspension (suspend_constitution) or its own ban (ban_party), the dispute is recorded as Withdrawn and the withdrawal price is charged. See reading R9.

implementation_readings.status: Claude's readings of the section-19 answers, written down before implementation so that nothing is chosen after a result is seen. They are not new design decisions. A reviewer or the user may overrule any of them before measurement, by a dated plan amendment (see 'amendments'). None was chosen with reference to seeds 0-11.
implementation_readings.R2_Q5:
Enforce re-tests acceptance at the current scope:
- on a Refused record, it closes as CompliedWhileOpen if acceptance >= .35, and otherwise becomes Enforced;
- on an Enforced record, it is accepted only when acceptance >= .35 (closing as CompliedWhileOpen), and is otherwise refused with "The order is already being enforced."
This gives an Enforced dispute at the narrowest scope an explicit path to compliance.
implementation_readings.R3_Q6:
(i) Powers are kept per (institution, scope) and are not nested: a complied wider scope does not save the narrower ones. Each scope's stake is consolidated at most once per institution, which bounds civilian-order consolidation at .05*(1/3+2/3+1) = .10 per institution, a leverage change of -.25.
(ii) Powers are cleared when regime_break runs army_seizure for the nation, the event that resets leverage to 1.0. Nothing else clears them. In a world without powers this writes nothing.
(iii) army_authority's module doc names a complied lawful civilian order as a third leverage path. Compliance does not change authoritarianism, as drafted.
implementation_readings.R5_Q10: A lapse receipt by the same issuer starts the cooldown, because a lapse is a closure. The cooldown is counted in clock::month_index, so the daily and monthly clocks agree.
implementation_readings.R6_Q12: The trigger is 'cannot pay this tick's upkeep in full' (pc < 0.20*dt) rather than pc == 0. With the existing floor-at-zero upkeep, a pc == 0 trigger closes one calendar month later on the monthly clock than on the daily one. The chosen trigger closes in the same calendar month on both clocks (I3).
implementation_readings.R7_Q13: The exact suffix text is "that ordered {phrase}". Before the change, a test checks that the headline is still counted as coup_el by a verbatim copy of the census rule (bloc_census.rs:377-398): it keeps the `COUP IN <NATION>:` prefix, contains `removes the elected government`, and does not contain `annuls the election`.
implementation_readings.R8_Q23: The new variant is named MandateLapsed and placed sixth, after InstitutionGone. Cases include interim status set by the scheduling seam and a restricted ballot ending an opening mandate. A ban by the issuer is handled by Q24 first.
implementation_readings.R9_Q24:
suspend_constitution and ban_party gain one hook before their own writes. When the nation's record passes the post-lapse view (so its issuer is the acting government), it is closed as Withdrawn:
- the withdrawal price (12 PC, ALWAYS, floored at 0) is charged in addition to the command's own price;
- it prints the withdrawal headline.
The hook covers player commands and AI levers alike, and writes nothing when there is no record.
implementation_readings.R10_Q11: The rescaling ratio is the ratio of the two Q4 gaps, set to 0 when gap_wide <= 0, as in Q11 above.
implementation_readings.R11_Q8: Rule 5's refusal sentence becomes: "{N}'s government holds neither an unrestricted completed ballot nor a sourced opening mandate; an interim or restricted mandate cannot order the armed forces."
implementation_readings.R12_Q1: Iteration is ordinals in stored order and, within each ordinal, scopes from widest to narrowest. The first legal, accepted and unsaved pair is issued.

coefficients.rule: Every coefficient is an invented design assumption, uncalibrated and never fitted to seeds 0-11. BUGS entries ('what would calibrate it', contract 7.6) are filed only after approval.

register.name: ARMY_PROGRAMME_VETO_WEIGHT (reused)
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: The approved programme-veto structure, loyalty - W*leverage*stake (22 Sep record). No new weight (Q16a).

register.name: scope stakes
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: Three evenly spaced steps from part to all of the Army's executive authority. The full order's stake equals the veto's maximum. A game abstraction with no source (Q15a).

register.name: compliance line ELECTORAL_COUP_ARMY (reused)
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: The hostile-Army line already shared by route 2 and the annulment.

register.name: AUTHORITY_CONSOLIDATION
register.value: 0.05 * stake via consolidate_transfer (leverage -0.125 * stake), once per saved (institution, scope)
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: The lawful-transfer amount (.05 per full term, government.rs lawful-transfer consolidation). A complied full order equals one full term of lawful transfer. Q6(b) bounds repeats.

register.name: AUTHORITY_ORDER_PC
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: Priced like CallElection (25), the other constitutional gamble open to an elected government (Q9a).

register.name: AUTHORITY_WITHDRAW_PC
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: ExpelFromGovernment's 12 PC: always available, never free (Q9a).

register.name: AUTHORITY_ENFORCEMENT_UPKEEP
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: upkeep = strain * 0.20 at one strain point, the floor cost of one coalition partner (Q9a). Unpayable upkeep lapses into a withdrawal (Q12b).

register.name: decision window
register.value: refusal month + the whole following calendar month
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: One full month for a player on either clock; the AI decides at its month-end review (Q17a).

register.name: escalation slope and cap (reused)
register.value: 0.60 per unit of gap per month; cap 1.5; gap capped at 0.45*leverage*s
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: Route 2's hostility slope 0.30*2. The Q4(b) cap keeps route 2's material term, and with it the D >= .25 guard, out of the dispute's gauge (Q4b, Q18a).

register.name: AUTHORITY_ORDER_COOLDOWN_MONTHS
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: ELECTORAL_COUP_SETTLED (12) reused as the minimum interval (Q10 a, d).

register.name: AI_ORDER_RESERVE_PC
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: The largest holding of the AI's other political-capital uses at the base (reading R4), so an order cannot starve them (Q9c). Derived from code thresholds, not from any outcome.

register.name: AI discontent line (reused)
register.label: invented design assumption
register.basis: ELECTORAL_COUP_DISCONTENT: a government does not pick a fight with its army in an economic crisis.

register.name: civilian-control guard
register.label: design-authority boundary, not a coefficient
register.basis: User decision D2 (4 Oct 2026; 22 Sep record), extended to D1 by Q7(a).

register.name: AUTHORITY_HISTORY_KEPT
register.label: engineering bound, not a model coefficient
register.basis: Save size. The cooldown reads only the newest receipt.

controls.as_written: Contract 14.2, controls 1-36, with the expected results the contract states, except where a decision changes them below. A control written for a drafted option takes the decided option.

changed_by_decision.5: Q11(b): a negotiation that still refuses returns to Refused with a new window, and the pressure is rescaled by gap_narrow/gap_wide. Nothing accrues while Refused.
changed_by_decision.6: Q9(a), Q10(a, d), Q21(a): withdrawal charges 12 PC ALWAYS (PC 5 gives 0) and leaves leverage unchanged. The same issuer is blocked for 12 months from closure and then allowed. A replaced issuer is not blocked.
changed_by_decision.8:
Q5(b), replacing the drafted control: take an Enforced dispute with pressure 1.49, and raise acceptance to >= .35 by funding.
- The dispute does not close, does not accrue, and does not fire.
- An explicit Enforce then closes it as CompliedWhileOpen, applying consolidate_transfer(.05*s) and saving the power.
- A Negotiate to an accepted narrower scope closes it as NegotiatedCompliance.
changed_by_decision.9: Q8(b): each case is refused with its sentence: a missing Army, a regime, an interim government, a restricted mandate without an attested opening mandate, and a record under 6 months.
changed_by_decision.21: Q13(b): the headline equals the suffixed template, with the recorded institution name. A verbatim copy of the census parse classifies it as coup_el.
changed_by_decision.24: Q1(a), Q9(c): the AI issues only orders whose plan says complies. It never issues one that will be refused. It never issues when D >= .25, without a majority, below 93 PC, inside the cooldown, for a saved scope, or for the player.
changed_by_decision.25: Q1(a): Withdraw is the only response. The AI never acts on the player's dispute, and the response is deterministic.
changed_by_decision.27: Q24(b): with an Enforced dispute and pressure 1.49, the issuer's own suspension, by the AI lever or by a player command, closes the dispute as Withdrawn in the same arm call and charges 12 PC ALWAYS, with no escalation. The issuer's own ban does the same. After a reopening with the same party: no dispute, no accrual, no firing.
changed_by_decision.32: Q10(d): the new government's own order is not blocked by the old issuer's cooldown. The arm first closes the old record as IssuerReplaced.
changed_by_decision.34: Q23(a): rule 5 or 6 lost while still electoral lapses the dispute as MandateLapsed. dispute_acceptance is Some on every validated record.
changed_by_decision.35: Q3(b): an actor with a lever plays the same lever, and an actor with a chosen card plays the same card, with the same draw sequence as on f6597cf5. The order is a candidate only when neither exists.

added.38: Q12(b): an Enforced dispute whose political capital is below the tick's upkeep closes as Withdrawn (PC goes to 0), with no accrual or firing that tick. The closure falls in the same calendar month on the daily and monthly clocks.
added.39: Q8(b): a government with an attested opening mandate and a six-month record may issue. It is refused without the marker, with a leader whose party is not attested, or under six months.
added.40: Q9(c): the AI never issues below 93 PC. AI_ORDER_RESERVE_PC is at least 55, 60, and the largest DECK cost + 20, computed from DECK.
added.41: Q4(b): with eff_k < .35, the month's accrual equals 0.60 * 0.45 * leverage * s * dt, never the full gap. With eff_k >= .35, it equals 0.60 * (0.35 - acceptance) * dt. When gap <= 0, nothing accrues.
added.42:
Q22(a): a dispute in a takeover-off world is frozen.
- The validation step, the tick and the regime_break hook read nothing.
- A maybe_coup break leaves the record unchanged.
- Resolutions are refused by the switch sentence.
- With the switch on again, validation runs first.

stop_and_report_rule.report: Every gate value is reported as measured, pass or fail, against the baseline, whether it improves, holds or regresses.
stop_and_report_rule.regression: Any original-gate regression (R13) or a failing Algeria chronology test is reported, and the candidate is rejected for integration. f6597cf5 stays the base, and every artifact is kept. The response never compensates: no change to any gate, country, coefficient, scope, price, timing, temperament, threshold, seed or cohort.
stop_and_report_rule.a1_fails_others_pass: Report a failure. A1 stays open. Q25 (keep the mechanic without A1 credit, or revert) goes back to the user.
stop_and_report_rule.all_pass: Report a pass. It does not close A1, CODEX-S27-A1-01, S27, G5 or CP1. The task stays blocked until a human-reviewed contract and the retained passing evidence both exist, and until CI confirms on both platforms.
stop_and_report_rule.bug_after_measurement: A demonstrated implementation bug found after measurement may be fixed. 'Demonstrated' means a deviation from this plan or the contract, shown by a focused failing test or by code against the text, and never inferred from a gate value alone. The fix changes no coefficient, threshold, scope, price, timing, temperament or other design choice. The gate is then measured once more on the fixed commit, and both results are kept and reported. The first result is never discarded or silently superseded.
stop_and_report_rule.design_change_after_measurement: None without a new user decision, which then needs a new predeclared plan.

amendments: Before the measurement command runs, this plan may be amended only by a dated, committed amendment that gives its reason. That covers a reviewer or the user overruling an implementation reading, or a defect found in the plan. No amendment may cite a seeds 0-11 political outcome; none will have been observed. After the measurement starts, the plan is not amended.
